correctness.rationale: PASS: Chvátal's perfect-graph description yields all halfspaces x_v≥0 and x(C)≤1 for maximal cliques. Both classes are facets: coordinate faces have affinely independent 0 and singletons except v; for maximal C, singleton e_c (c∈C) plus stable pair e_u+e_{c(u)} for each u∉C with c(u) nonadjacent to u yield |V| affinely independent on x(C)=1. A Euclidean radius-r ball at center c is contained exactly when c_v≥r and c(C)+r sqrt(|C|)≤1. A maximum clique and c_v≥r force r≤1/(ω+sqrt ω). Uniform c=r*1 attains all inequalities since k+sqrt k increases with k. At r*, these inequalities themselves give the complete incenter set. Every maximum clique forces c_v=r* on its vertices; hence unique iff all vertices are in max cliques, otherwise a vertex outside every maximum clique has finite positive slack and can be perturbed. At the uniform incenter every coordinate facet and only maximum clique facets touch. Algebraically invert r* to recover ω and, for perfect G, χ. The n=1 and edgeless graph boundaries satisfy the argument. Small independent instances corroborated, not proof.
